original_test_intent: Conditionally test deletion of one explicitly approved, non-built-in Redfish role only after the owner corrects the GET/DELETE mismatch and proves target identity, dependency impact, implementation support, continued recovery access and exact recreation.
original_method: Preserve the source conflict and prohibit DeepSeek's placeholder DELETE; after a corrected contract, baseline the role and dependents, execute one approved delete, verify absence/access health and recreate only through the independently validated recovery procedure.
manual_activity: The security/BMC owner resolves GET versus DELETE, authorizes a specific non-critical role, confirms all account/service dependencies, supplies vendor deletion semantics and an exact independently tested recreation/recovery path, and approves the maintenance window.
required_inputs: Corrected testcase or owner ruling on GET versus DELETE
Exact role identity and proof it is not built-in/core
Recovery account or console independent of target role
safety_requirements: Do not proceed with active required dependents
One DELETE with no automatic retry
Prove independent recovery and exact recreation before deletion
No unrelated account or privilege changes
agent_execution_scope: Bind endpoint and inventory exact role/dependents
Capture immutable role/OEM/privilege baseline and concurrency token
Validate vendor delete and recreation contracts offline
Present exact DELETE and impact for approval
Verify member absence and collection/dependency state
engineer_actions: Resolve source conflict and approve exact non-critical role
Approve dependency impact, recovery access and recreation proof

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The placeholder DELETE is not authorized by the GET-only Master, provides no built-in/dependency/recreation safeguards, uses unsafe transport/credential handling and cannot be executed.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not expose a DELETE until the owner supplies a corrected target and independently validated recreation package. Then use trusted secret-safe access to delete that exact role once, verify absence and access health, and recreate only through the approved recovery plan.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The role-member resource family and 15/10 timing remain; exact target, deletion semantics, acceptable dependencies and recovery are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat role deletion as a dependency-aware authorization migration: freeze an exact reconstructable baseline, prove alternate recovery, delete one approved non-core role, validate absence/dependents and restore deterministically if the test requires it.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an authoritative DELETE contract and independently viable recreation instead of converting a copied GET into an irreversible placeholder operation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Member/collection GETs can inventory the role and links but cannot establish DELETE authorization, dependent-account behavior, absence semantics or recreation fidelity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Deleting an assigned or vendor/core role can strand accounts, remove privileges or make the original object impossible to recreate; rollback claims are invalid unless schema/OEM fields and creation support are proven beforehand.

project_override_considerations: A vendor role manager is acceptable only if its deletion and recreation semantics are documented, target/dependency identity is preserved, alternate recovery is independent and exact before/after authorization evidence is retained.
expected_evidence: Owner-approved corrected DELETE scope and exact role identity
Proof target is non-built-in and complete dependent-account/service inventory
Immutable endpoint, certificate trust and secret-safe session
Complete redacted role/privilege/OEM recreation baseline and concurrency token
Post-delete absence, collection and dependency/access results
Approved recreation request and exact restored-state comparison if invoked

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title says Delete Role, but the Master Procedure only GETs one role and Criteria assess readability/success. It defines no DELETE target authorization, absence result, dependency behavior or recreation. DeepSeek's placeholder DELETE is not authoritative.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An owner/vendor artifact can resolve the target, delete support, dependencies and exact recreation. Execution remains prohibited until those prerequisites are supplied; if recreation or safe recovery stays indeterminate after authoritative artifacts, execution must then be classified BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Makes the destructive source conflict explicit and requires a non-core dependency-safe target plus independently validated recreation before any deletion can occur.
independent_technical_reasoning: A 404 after DELETE is not sufficient success: the role may still be referenced by accounts, may be a vendor/core authorization object, or may be impossible to recreate with identical OEM and privilege semantics. Because the Master never specifies DELETE, target selection and recovery cannot come from a placeholder. Safe execution requires proving an alternate recovery identity that does not depend on the role, freezing every reconstructable field, and verifying both dependent access and exact restored state.
